question: Pipe P can fill (5)/(7) part of a tank in 30 hours, and pipe Q can fill (2)/(5) part of the same tank in 28 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 7 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 8 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time to fill tank: P = 30 × 7/5 = 42 hours, Q = 28 × 5/2 = 70 hours.

Total capacity = LCM(42, 70) = 210 units ⇒ P's efficiency = 5 units/hr, Q's efficiency = 3 units/hr.

Volume filled by P and Q in 7 hours = (5 + 3) × 7 = 56 units.

R empties 56 units in 8 hours ⇒ R's efficiency = −56 ÷ 8 = −7 units/hr.

Time taken by P, Q, and R together = 210 ÷ (5 + 3 − 7) = 210 ÷ 1 = 210 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 210 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Pipe P can fill 5/7 part of a tank in 30 hours.

Pipe Q can fill 2/5 part of the same tank in 28 hours.

Both P and Q were kept open for 7 hours, then closed.

Pipe R empties the filled water in 8 hours.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total time taken by P to fill the complete tank = 30 × (7/5) = 42 hours.

⇒ Total time taken by Q to fill the complete tank = 28 × (5/2) = 70 hours.

⇒ Work done by Pipe P and Pipe Q together in 7 hours = (5 + 3) × 7 = 8 × 7 = 56 units.

⇒ The tank has 56 units of water when P and Q are closed.

⇒ Pipe R alone empties these 56 units in 8 hours.

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe R = −56 ÷ 8 = −7 units/hour.

⇒ Net efficiency when Pipes P, Q, and R are opened together = 5 + 3 − 7 = 1 unit/hour.

⇒ Time taken by P, Q, and R together to fill the empty tank = Total Work ÷ Net efficiency.

⇒ Time taken = 210 ÷ 1 = 210 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 210 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency Rule

When a pipe fills a tank, its efficiency is taken as positive. When a pipe (or leak) empties a tank, its efficiency is taken as negative.

LCM Method

The total capacity of the tank is assumed to be the LCM of the time taken by individual pipes to fill or empty the tank completely. Efficiency = Total Capacity ÷ Time Taken.

Combined Work

If multiple pipes are operating together, their combined net efficiency is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies: Combined Efficiency = E₁ + E₂ − E₃.
